title: Review cook mode feature integration
description: Perform a final integration review across CookbookCore, recipe-detail entry, cook-mode UI flow, tests, and documentation, with attention to regressions, dependency ordering, and any unresolved product decisions called out by the spec.
acceptance_criteria: Review confirms implementation matches the spec's in-scope behavior and flags any deviations such as disabled-versus-hidden button treatment or counter styling choices.
Review covers regression risk around recipe detail behavior, idle-timer restoration, step flattening, and scale carry-over.
Review verifies shared tests and documentation landed against the final implementation state before sign-off.

handoff_summary.completed: Reviewed all 10 source files (CookModeView.swift, CookModeStepView.swift, CookModeIngredientList.swift, RecipeBottomBar.swift, RecipeDetailSheet.swift, Recipe.swift, CookModeViewTests.swift, RecipeBottomBarTests.swift, StepTests.swift, docs/architecture.md). Verified scale locking, idle-timer restoration, step flattening, double-scaling avoidance, disabled-button treatment, fullScreenCover wiring, and architecture doc completeness.
handoff_summary.remaining: One finding requires a corrective fix: CookModeDonePage must suppress the navigation bar (add .toolbar(.hidden, for: .navigationBar)) so that only the in-page Done button is visible on the completion page, matching the stated design decision. Administrative: spec file should be moved from drafts to done once the corrective is resolved.
handoff_summary.risks: Low. The outstanding finding is cosmetic only — both the Close and Done buttons dismiss the full-screen cover identically. No functional regression, data loss, or session-state issue. The fix is a one-line modifier addition.
handoff_summary.next_action: Add .toolbar(.hidden, for: .navigationBar) to CookModeDonePage in CookbookApp/Recipes/CookModeStepView.swift:157, then re-run review to confirm the finding is resolved.
handoff_summary.block_reason: CookModeDonePage (CookModeStepView.swift:157) does not suppress the parent NavigationStack toolbar's Close button. The design decision states explicitly: CookModeDonePage hides the nav bar controls and presents its own Done button. Fix: add .toolbar(.hidden, for: .navigationBar) to CookModeDonePage.body or as a view modifier on the struct's view return. Both buttons currently dismiss the cover identically, so there is no functional regression, but the deviation from the documented design decision must be resolved before sign-off.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None identified. Fix is additive (one modifier on a private struct). No file overlap with other in-flight beads.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: All other design decisions validated: scale locked at init via recipe.scaled(by:), no double-scaling (CookModeIngredientList uses scale:.one for pre-scaled content), disabled-not-hidden button treatment for Cook now, idle timer managed via onAppear/onDisappear, RecipeStepCombiner used for step text resolution, section title shown in page content (not nav bar title), step counter in bottom bar only, GatherIngredientsPhase as private struct in CookModeView.swift.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: StepTests covers ingredientIndices() deduplication and ordering. CookModeViewTests covers view instantiation, StepsPhase instantiation, done-page indexing, navigation boundary conditions, and free-text skipping. RecipeBottomBarTests covers hasSteps/hasIngredients gating, disabled conditions, and callback invocability. All tests verify underlying logic conditions rather than SwiftUI render state — consistent with the stated testing pattern for @State-private views.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: No automated test for CookModeDonePage toolbar visibility (SwiftUI render state is not testable via @testable import). The corrective fix should be verified by manual review. Spec file specs/drafts/cook-mode-guided-step-by-step-recipe-workflow.md is absent from the worktree — should be moved to specs/done/ once the corrective is merged.

conflict_risks: None identified. Fix is additive (one modifier on a private struct). No file overlap with other in-flight beads.

guardrails.template_text:
# Review Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Inspect code, tests, docs, and acceptance criteria for correctness, completeness, and risk.

Allowed actions:
- Review only the changed files listed in the bead's touched_files and changed_files fields. Do not read unrelated files.
- Validate acceptance criteria against the implementation and handoff state.
- Block with a clear recommendation when the bead actually requires implementation work.

Efficiency constraints:
- Do not run the test suite. Testing is the tester agent's responsibility.
- Focus on correctness, completeness, and risk — not style or formatting.
- Keep the review concise. If there are no findings, say so and approve promptly.

Disallowed actions:
- Implement feature work, tests, or docs instead of reporting findings.
- Rewrite architecture or silently fix issues discovered during review.
- Mark incomplete work as accepted without evidence.

Expected outputs:
- Return JSON with `outcome` set to `completed` (reviews always complete; use `verdict` for pass/fail) and `summary` as a one-line description of the review result.
- Return JSON with structured verdict fields for every run: `verdict`, `findings_count`, and `requires_followup`.
- Treat `verdict` as the review signoff decision: `approved` means the bead can complete, while `needs_changes` means the bead must block for follow-up work.
- Use `verdict=approved`, `findings_count=0`, and `requires_followup=false` when no unresolved findings remain.
- Use `verdict=needs_changes`, set `findings_count` to the unresolved finding count, set `requires_followup=true` unless there is a stronger explicit reason not to, and always include `block_reason` when any required fix remains.
- Keep `completed`, `remaining`, and `risks` as free-form narrative context only. They inform operators, but they do not override the structured verdict or control scheduler state.
- Review findings ordered by severity, or an explicit statement that no findings were discovered.
- Clear blocked handoff details when the task belongs to another agent type.
